-- Converted: CREATE USER analyst -> CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS ANALYST TYPE = PERSON with DEFAULT_ROLE = READER; removed PASSWORD, PERM = 0, FROM sales and DEFAULT DATABASE
-- Reason: Plaintext passwords must not be embedded (snowflake.security.no_plaintext_credentials) — set credentials out-of-band or via SSO; PERM space and the FROM owner hierarchy have no Snowflake equivalent; DEFAULT_ROLE points the user at the role granted to it
CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS ANALYST
  TYPE = PERSON
  DEFAULT_ROLE = READER
  COMMENT = 'Migrated from Teradata user analyst (DEFAULT DATABASE = sales)';

assumptions: Teradata database `sales` maps to Snowflake schema SALES in the current deployment database, per the naming map (two-part names).
Teradata default NOT CASESPECIFIC VARCHAR/CHAR comparisons become case-sensitive in Snowflake; no collation added — review queries that relied on case-insensitive matching.

customer_id is the business key of CUSTOMER: SALES."ACCOUNT" declares a FOREIGN KEY to it, and Snowflake (like Teradata) requires the referenced columns to be a PRIMARY KEY/UNIQUE constraint; the added PK is informational (NOT ENFORCED, NORELY by default).
explanations: SET TABLE converted to a standard Snowflake table using the naming-map name SALES.CUSTOMER.
PRIMARY INDEX removed: distribution is automatic in Snowflake; add CLUSTER BY only if the table grows to multi-TB and is filtered on the PI columns.
CHAR(1) DEFAULT 'A' kept; Snowflake CHAR is stored without trailing-blank padding, which is identical for single-character values.
NOT NULL constraints kept (Snowflake enforces NOT NULL); the added PRIMARY KEY is metadata only and does not reject duplicates.

-- Converted: SET TABLE -> standard permanent table; dropped PRIMARY INDEX (customer_id); INTEGER/BIGINT kept as Snowflake INTEGER/BIGINT (aliases of NUMBER(38,0), a superset of Teradata int32/int64 range); DECIMAL(p,s) kept as NUMBER(p,s); added informational CONSTRAINT PK_CUSTOMER PRIMARY KEY (customer_id)
-- Reason: Snowflake has no SET/MULTISET table kinds; all tables allow duplicate rows; Teradata PRIMARY INDEX controls AMP hash distribution; Snowflake partitions storage automatically and recommends clustering keys only for very large tables, so no CLUSTER BY is added; the PK lets SALES."ACCOUNT" declare its FOREIGN KEY (Snowflake requires referenced PK/UNIQUE) and is not enforced so results are unchanged
CREATE TABLE SALES.CUSTOMER (
  customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  customer_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
  status CHAR(1) DEFAULT 'A',
  CONSTRAINT PK_CUSTOMER PRIMARY KEY (customer_id)
);

-- Reason: MULTISET already allows duplicates, matching Snowflake; Teradata PRIMARY INDEX controls AMP hash distribution; Snowflake partitions storage automatically and recommends clustering keys only for very large tables, so no CLUSTER BY is added; ACCOUNT is a Snowflake reserved word so the naming map requires the quoted identifier "ACCOUNT"
CREATE TABLE SALES."ACCOUNT" (
  account_id BIGINT NOT NULL,
  customer_id INTEGER CONSTRAINT FK_ACCOUNT_CUSTOMER REFERENCES SALES.CUSTOMER (customer_id),
  balance NUMBER(14,2) DEFAULT 0
);

unsupported: FOREIGN KEY referential integrity is not enforced on Snowflake standard tables (the constraint is kept as metadata only); orphan customer_id values will not be rejected.
